claim: Cat Museum founded 1993, owned by DBKU, 4,000+ exhibits, holds Bay cat specimen and a mummified Egyptian cat
quote: Founded in 1993... owned by Kuching North City Hall (DBKU)... over 4,000 artifacts... the only preserved specimen of the world's rarest cat, the Bay cat (Felis badia)... a mummified cat from ancient Egypt

claim: The Cat Museum is the first museum in the world dedicated entirely to cats, fitting for cat-named Kuching
quote: the first museum in the world built to showcase entirely on cats

claim: The 2.5m Great Cat of Kuching ('Nick') is dressed in costumes for festivals; city has a cat fountain and a rafflesia-topped cat column
quote: The white cat with wire whiskers called Nick is dressed up in traditional attire during major festivals - red for Chinese New Year, green during Eid ul Fitr, Santa clothes during Christmas and a traditional Iban vest during the local harvest festival

claim: Kuching has a trail of kitschy cat statues scattered across the city
quote: Travelling to Kuching? Catch the 7 kitschy cat statues there

claim: The origin of the name Kuching is disputed; the cat theory is doubtful because Sarawak Malays use 'pusak' not 'kucing' for cat
quote: ethnic Malays in Sarawak have always used the term 'pusak' for cats instead of the standard Malay word 'kucing'

claim: Competing theories for the name include Cat River, Chinese 'old well', mata kucing fruit and the port term Cochin
quote: Neither Pussy Nor Well - Origins of the name of Kuching

claim: Meow Meow Cat Cafe, established 2014, charges RM10 for unlimited time in the cat area
quote: Established in 2014, this cozy cafe... For an entry fee of RM10, visitors can spend unlimited time in the cat area

claim: The Upside Down Museum has rooms built upside down for photo ops; ranks among Kuching's quirky picks
quote: Head to the Upside Down Museum for some fun photo opportunities... rooms designed to look like they're flipped upside down

claim: Fairland Hidden Bar serves Sarawak's first freshly brewed craft beer with a hidden back-alley street-food scene
quote: Sarawak's very first freshly brewed craft beer... hidden back alley with delicious street food

claim: Drunk Monkey Old Street Bar is a vintage bar on one of Kuching's oldest streets near the river
quote: a unique vintage bar located on one of the oldest streets in Kuching near the river

claim: Kuching's bar scene includes hidden and underground venues like PlanB Hidden Bar in the Galacity area
quote: The 10 Best bars in Kuching (2026 ranked)

claim: Black Bean Coffee home-roasts local beans; its signature is the Iced Gula Apong Latte and it enforces a one-hour seating limit
quote: Black Bean Coffee - Old-school cafe serving locally roasted Sarawak beans; signature drink is the Iced Gula Apong Latte. One-hour seating limit enforces authentic vintage atmosphere

claim: Black Bean Coffee is a quirky old-school shop serving home-roasted Sarawak coffee
quote: Black Bean Coffee is a quirky, old-school coffee shop serving the best authentic Sarawak coffee in town, with coffee beans sourced locally and home-roasted

claim: A hidden alley between India Street and Electra House has been turned into an outdoor mural gallery
quote: a quiet alley tucked between India Street and Electra House in downtown Kuching... transformed into a lively outdoor gallery where walls come alive with vibrant murals

claim: Most of Kuching's official murals were painted by local artist Leonard Siaw; best clusters are in the old bazaar streets
quote: Most of the official street art were painted by Kuching-born Leonard Siaw

claim: The Indian Mosque is Kuching's oldest mosque, built of belian ironwood by Tamil Muslim traders, hidden in laneways
quote: Kuching's oldest mosque stands as a modest structure built of belian (ironwood)... built by Muslim traders from Tamil Nadu

claim: The mosque is reached via tiny Indian Mosque Lane (Lg Sempit) off India Street, so hidden most outsiders miss it
quote: so well hidden in the laneways and alleyways that few outsiders notice the original building until it is pointed out to them by local people

claim: Bako is Sarawak's oldest national park and home to roughly 150 endangered proboscis monkeys plus bearded pigs and silvered langurs
quote: Bako is home to approximately 150 endangered proboscis monkeys, endemic to Borneo

claim: Bako's largest mammal is the bearded pig (seen around HQ); nocturnal residents include the colugo flying lemur, tarsier and slow loris
quote: The largest mammal found at Bako is the Bornean Bearded Pig... Bako's nocturnal creatures include the flying lemur, pangolin, mouse deer, various bats, tarsier, slow loris and palm civet

claim: Bako is 37 km from Kuching, reached by a short boat ride; last boat back leaves at 3pm so day trips need an early start
quote: Bako National Park is just 37 kilometers from Kuching... the last boat back leaving at 3pm

claim: The fanged pitcher plant N. bicalcarata has two 3cm spines under the lid and lives in mutualism with Camponotus schmitzi ants in Sarawak peat swamp
quote: The two sharp spines for which the species is famous are present on the underside of the pitcher lid, and may be 3 cm long... mutualistic relationship with Camponotus schmitzi ants

claim: Kubah (45 min from Kuching) has rare pitcher plants and 60+ frog species, including the tiny Matang narrow-mouth frog that breeds in pitcher plants
quote: the smallest species of frog in the world - the Matang narrow mouth frog, which lives inside and around pitcher plants

claim: Guided night 'frogging' walks at Kubah head up Summit Road to the frog pond to spot dozens of frog species
quote: Frogging at Kubah National Park

claim: Evening Santubong river cruises show fireflies lighting the mangroves like Christmas lights
quote: Fireflies illuminate the mangroves with soft, rhythmic flashes... their synchronized glow creates an enchanting spectacle

claim: The Santubong cruise also offers chances to see Irrawaddy dolphins, proboscis monkeys and crocodiles before the firefly display
quote: wildlife often seen on this cruise includes Irrawaddy dolphins, proboscis monkeys, crocodiles, silver-leaf monkeys, fireflies

claim: Semenggoh (24 km from Kuching) rehabilitates 20+ semi-wild orangutans with feedings at 9am and 3pm
quote: twice daily feedings at 9 am... and 3 pm... More than 20 orangutans inhabit this protected forest

claim: Orangutan sightings at Semenggoh are not guaranteed; during fruiting season they forage in the forest and may skip feedings
quote: During the fruiting season, orangutans may not appear, as they prefer foraging naturally in the forest. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed

claim: Satok Weekend Market (Medan Niaga Satok) showcases jungle produce, exotic fruits and fresh seafood, liveliest Sat afternoon/Sun morning
quote: Satok Market... showcasing an impressive array of jungle produce, exotic fruits, and fresh seafood

claim: Satok sells weird-and-wonderful forest produce: ferns, wild honey, home-grown spices, orchids and fruits found only on Borneo
quote: the forest vendors' weird and wonderful produce, including fruits only found on Borneo... jungle produce from ferns to wild honey, plus animals, orchids

claim: Kek lapis Sarawak is dyed in vivid colours and cut/reassembled into kaleidoscopic patterns echoing indigenous tribal motifs
quote: cutting the cake into logs before reassembling those logs to form intricate designs reminiscent of indigenous tribe motifs... a kaleidoscope of colored layers

claim: A 2026 luxury 'Kek Lapis Sultan' sells for RM1,800 per tray and each takes about eight hours to bake layer by layer
quote: ten-layer 'Luxury Kek Lapis Sultan', priced at RM1,800 per tray... Each tray takes about eight hours to produce

claim: Maria Kek Lapis is a well-known Kuching shop selling elaborate layer cakes
quote: MARIA KEK LAPIS, Kuching

claim: Sarawak specialities include midin jungle fern, raw-fish umai, dabai fruit and tuak rice-wine ice cream
quote: their special dessert: ice cream with tuak (local rice wine)... Nasi goreng dabai is rice stir-fried with dabai... an indigenous fruit found only in Sarawak

claim: Sarawak Laksa ranked in Anthony Bourdain's Top 10 and was named TasteAtlas best dish in Asia (2021)
quote: ranking in the Top 10 by world-renowned chef Anthony Bourdain... Sarawak Laksa was named the best dish in Asia according to readers' feedback on TasteAtlas

claim: Top Spot Food Court sits on the roof of a multi-storey car park on Jalan Padungan, famed for pick-your-own live seafood and umai
quote: located atop a multi-storey car park in Jalan Padungan, Kuching, is a legendary rooftop food street destination... famed for its live seafood selection

claim: Kuching was named a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2021, the first in Malaysia; umai is a raw-fish Melanau dish
quote: In 2021, Kuching was recognised by UNESCO as a Creative City of Gastronomy, becoming the first city in Malaysia to receive the accolade

claim: Tuak is Sarawak's indigenous glutinous-rice wine, central to Dayak ritual and now reaching new audiences
quote: Malaysia's Indigenous Rice Wine Is Reaching New Audiences

claim: Small Sarawak brewers host tuak tastings and demos of the brewing process at their studios and pop-ups
quote: Producers host tasting and drink events and show demos of the tuak process at their studios

claim: Gawai Dayak harvest festival falls on 1 June; tuak is the customary welcome drink, with celebrations at Annah Rais and Kampung Benuk
quote: A welcome drink of 'tuak' (rice wine) is the order of the day during Gawai celebrations

claim: The Brooke Gallery (opened 2016) tells the story of Sarawak and its 'White Rajahs'
quote: The Brooke Gallery tells the story of one of the most remarkable kingdoms in history: Sarawak and its 'White Rajahs'

claim: Fort Margherita was built in 1879 by Rajah Charles Brooke in the style of an English castle, named after his wife Margaret
quote: Built by the second Rajah, Sir Charles Brooke, in 1879, the design of this iconic landmark is based on an English castle. He named it after his wife, Margaret Alice Lili de Windt

claim: The traditional penambang/tambang boat has crossed the Sarawak River since the Brooke era and costs RM1 per trip
quote: has been around since the Brooke era... The fare is currently RM1 per passenger, up from 30 cents in the 1990s

claim: The Wallace Centre celebrates Alfred Russel Wallace's 1854-56 Sarawak stay, when he wrote the 'Sarawak Law' on the origin of species
quote: celebrates the work of the naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace during his stay in Sarawak from 1854 to 1856... wrote his famous 'The Sarawak Law' paper

claim: Wallace drafted the Sarawak Law near Kuching, an early stepping-stone to the theory of evolution by natural selection
quote: Wallace and the Sarawak Law

claim: Borneo Cultures Museum, opened March 2022, is the largest museum in Malaysia and second-largest in Southeast Asia, five floors
quote: the largest museum in Malaysia and the second largest in Southeast Asia... spanning 6,726 square meters of exhibition space across five floors

claim: The Borneo Cultures Museum sits beside Padang Merdeka in central Kuching with modern interactive exhibits
quote: Borneo Cultures Museum - Sarawak Museum Department

claim: Hong San Si Temple on Carpenter Street has existed since 1848, dedicated to Hokkien child deity Kong Teck Choon Ong
quote: a Chinese temple situated in Carpenter Street... existed since 1848, and is dedicated to Hokkien child deity Kong Teck Choon Ong

claim: Tua Pek Kong is the oldest temple in Kuching, on the waterfront, part of the Kuching Heritage Trail
quote: the oldest temple in the city and formed a part of the Kuching Heritage Trail

claim: The S-shaped Darul Hana pedestrian bridge opened November 2017, spans 335m with horn-shaped towers and nightly LED shows
quote: an elegant S-shaped pedestrian bridge that officially opened in November 2017... Spanning 335 meters, the bridge features twin horn-shaped towers

claim: Annah Rais is a living Bidayuh longhouse offering day visits and homestays with traditional bamboo-chicken meals
quote: Annah Rais Longhouse Adventure... a genuine homestay and an eye-opening cultural experience

claim: Annah Rais Longhouse Homestay is about 60 km / one hour from Kuching
quote: Annah Rais Longhouse Homestay is located 60km from Kuching City and takes approximately one hour drive

claim: Annah Rais is a ~200-year-old bamboo-and-wood longhouse of the former headhunting Land Dayaks, with skull relics on display
quote: Annah Rais Longhouse: A Surviving Bidayuh Longhouse

claim: Fairy Cave (Gua Pari) near Bau is a show cave reached by stairs, with Taoist shrines among limestone formations
quote: Fairy Caves... feature mesmerizing limestone formations, lush vegetation, and the intriguing presence of Taoist shrines and altars

claim: Wind Cave has a plankwalk through a bat-filled limestone outcrop; Fairy Cave closes Mondays, Wind Cave Tuesdays
quote: Fairy Cave is closed every Monday and Wind Cave is closed every Tuesday

claim: Bau is a former gold-mining town ~26 km from Kuching with the Tasik Biru Blue Lake nearby
quote: Bau is a rural town you can drive to from Kuching city, with nearby natural wonders including the Fairy Cave, the Wind Cave, and the Tasik Biru Blue Lake

claim: Semadang Kayak runs day trips on the upper Sarawak River in Padawan (~40 km from Kuching) with rapids, swimming and waterfalls
quote: eco-friendly way to experience the pristine beauty of the Sarawak River in the Semadang area, about 40 km from Kuching

claim: Semadang kayaking is promoted as a beginner-friendly half- or full-day outdoor adventure near Kuching
quote: Semadang Kayak Adventure

claim: Sarawak pottery, made by Teochew Chinese families on Jalan Penrissen, blends Chinese forms with Dayak designs and colours
quote: the originally-Chinese pottery products were adapted to incorporate traditional Dayak designs and colours

claim: The Jalan Penrissen (5th Mile) pottery workshops are a fading traditional trade where visitors can watch potters work
quote: ENDANGERED TRADES: THE POTTER'S HAND

claim: The Rainforest World Music Festival 2026 runs 26-28 June at the Sarawak Cultural Village below Mount Santubong
quote: Rainforest World Music Festival 2026 | June 26-28, Sarawak

claim: The 29th RWMF carries the 2026 theme 'Regenerations: Roots & Rhythms' with daytime workshops and evening main-stage concerts
quote: the theme 'Regenerations: Roots & Rhythms'

claim: Bako has around 275 proboscis monkeys and 16 marked trails through rainforest, sea cliffs and beaches
quote: Approximately 275 proboscis monkeys live in Bako... The park's 16 well-marked trails wind through lush rainforests, past dramatic sea cliffs, and cross golden beaches
